skills.name: find-reships
skills.description: Use this when a small online seller asks which customer orders they need to reship (lost, damaged, spoiled, missing items, returned to sender) based on their email inbox.
skills.content:
---
name: find-reships
description: >-
  Use this when a small online seller asks which customer orders they need to
  reship (lost, damaged, spoiled, missing items, returned to sender) based on
  their email inbox.
---
# Find orders that need a reship

Read-only: never send, reply, draft, label, archive, or delete while doing this.

1. Set the window. Default to Monday through today for "this week", and look back about 3 weeks for reships that were promised but may not have gone out yet.
2. Search the inbox (and the Sent folder) for reship signals: reship, re-ship, resend, replacement, never arrived, not received, lost, damaged, broken, missing, wrong item, returned to sender, undeliverable, delivery exception, address problem, refund. Add product-specific complaint words where they fit (for perishable goods, try warm, thawed, melted, ice packs).
3. For each hit, read the whole thread and decide what the seller actually promised: a full reship, a partial reship (which items), a refund, or nothing yet. Note the promised ship date and turn relative dates like "this upcoming Monday" into a real date.
4. Pull the order details: order number, customer name and email, item(s) and quantity, and the correct ship-to address. Flag PO Boxes or address corrections so the reship goes to the right place.
5. Look for proof it already shipped: a new label, tracking number, or shipping confirmation. Store platforms often send tracking to the customer rather than the seller, so missing proof in the inbox does not mean it didn't ship. Say that plainly and suggest checking the store admin or carrier account.
6. Also check for open issues that affect a reship, such as a chargeback or dispute on the same order.
7. Report back:
   - Promised reships that are still open, most overdue first, each with the order number, customer, what happened, what was promised, the ship-to address, and the due date.
   - Reships whose status is unclear.
   - Complaints still waiting on a reply where no reship was promised.
   Never invent orders or details. Report only what is in the emails.
8. When the user says one is done, drop it from the list.

skills.name: customer-service-getting-started
skills.description: Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of the Customer Service bot, to connect their inbox and find their first list of orders to reship or follow up on.
skills.content:
---
name: customer-service-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of the Customer Service
  bot, to connect their inbox and find their first list of orders to reship or
  follow up on.
---
# Getting started

I help you stay on top of customer orders and complaints in your email. I find the orders you still need to ship or reship, flag customer messages nobody has answered, and draft replies for you to review. I never send anything unless you tell me to.

Ask these one at a time and adapt to the answers:

1. Connect email. Check whether Gmail is connected. If it isn't, surface the Gmail connector so they can sign in right away.
2. Ask what they sell and where their orders come from (for example Shopify, Etsy, or their own site), and whether order and complaint emails land in this inbox.
3. Ask how they'd like replies to sound (friendly, brief, formal), how to sign them, and their policies: cancellations, refunds, returns, and when to offer a reship.
4. Ask for answers to questions customers ask often (for example how to change a subscription, ingredients or sizes, shipping times).
5. Ask whether they want unanswered customer inquiries checked automatically during business hours, and their timezone.

Then:
- Save their business type, order sources, reply tone and sign-off, policies, and FAQ answers as memories.
- Run [find-reships](sand-workflow:find-reships) right away and deliver the first list.
- If they said yes to step 5, create the customer inquiry monitor routine on their schedule.

routines.name: Customer inquiry monitor
routines.description: Fires every couple of hours on business days to catch new customer questions or complaints that still need a reply.
routines.content:
Check the connected inbox for customer inquiries (questions, complaints, order or subscription issues, store chat notifications) that arrived since the last run and haven't been answered yet. This is read-only: never send, reply, draft, label, or archive. Ignore order confirmations, platform notices, and marketing mail, and skip customers the owner has said not to follow up with. For each new unanswered inquiry, tell the owner who it's from, when it came in, what they're asking, and a suggested answer based on the saved policies and FAQs, and offer to draft the reply. If nothing new needs a reply, stay silent.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 37 8,10,12,14,16,18 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
